title: Grade 4 CREATIVE ARTS — Premium Revision Paper #7

pages.quiz:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #7
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. On a xylophone, the short bars give (1 mark)
   A. low notes
   B. high notes
   C. the loudest sound only
   D. no sound

2. What is the length of a full netball court? (1 mark)
   A. 10 metres
   B. 30.5 metres
   C. 100 metres
   D. 50 metres

3. How should a good netball player treat the other team at the end? (1 mark)
   A. Ignore them
   B. Tease them
   C. Shout at them
   D. Shake hands and thank them

4. What does pivoting mean? (1 mark)
   A. Dropping the ball
   B. Running quickly
   C. Turning on the landing foot without moving it
   D. Jumping over the ball

5. Which is a rule break in netball? (1 mark)
   A. Pivoting on one foot
   B. Pushing another player
   C. Catching with two hands
   D. Passing to a teammate

6. How is flour paste made? (1 mark)
   A. Freeze flour
   B. Mix flour and cold water to a smooth paste, then add hot water while stirring
   C. Mix flour and sand
   D. Burn flour

7. Colour value means (1 mark)
   A. how light or dark a colour is
   B. the smell of paint
   C. the price of a colour
   D. how loud a colour is

8. Which of these letters has neither an ascender nor a descender? (1 mark)
   A. a
   B. b
   C. p
   D. d

9. Rhythm is (1 mark)
   A. the loudness of the singer
   B. the name of the song
   C. the pattern of long and short sounds
   D. how high a note is

10. A rest is a sign for (1 mark)
   A. silence
   B. the loudest sound
   C. a repeat
   D. a song title

11. How many guide lines are used for practising lettering in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Four
   B. Two
   C. Six
   D. Ten

12. Which letter has a descender? (1 mark)
   A. k
   B. g
   C. a
   D. e

13. Stepwise motion means the tune moves (1 mark)
   A. by big jumps
   B. only on one note
   C. down only
   D. to the next note above or below

14. The Kodaly hand sign for m is (1 mark)
   A. a wave
   B. a flat palm held level
   C. a closed fist
   D. a sloping palm

15. The Kodaly hand sign for r is (1 mark)
   A. a flat hand held level
   B. a wave
   C. a sloping palm
   D. a closed fist

16. Which is the lowest of the notes d, r and m? (1 mark)
   A. They are all the same
   B. m
   C. r
   D. d

17. How do you make a coil? (1 mark)
   A. Cut it flat
   B. Roll a small piece between the palms or on a table
   C. Beat it with a stick
   D. Bake it

18. In a medium start, the rear knee is level with (1 mark)
   A. the heel of the front foot
   B. the middle of the front foot
   C. the start line
   D. the toe of the back foot

19. Why should the flag stick be held high when cheering? (1 mark)
   A. So it does not hit anyone
   B. To make noise
   C. To hide the runners
   D. To block the sun

20. How should we treat the national flag? (1 mark)
   A. Throw it around
   B. Write on it
   C. With care and respect, never letting it touch the ground
   D. Use it as a rag

21. What should you do after crossing the finish line? (1 mark)
   A. Stop suddenly
   B. Turn around fast
   C. Push others
   D. Slow down gradually

22. Which is the correct first step in the crab balance? (1 mark)
   A. Jump high
   B. Lie face down
   C. Sit with knees bent and feet flat
   D. Stand on your head

23. Where should you place your hands in a crab balance? (1 mark)
   A. On your head
   B. Behind you, shoulder-width apart
   C. In your pockets
   D. In front of your face

24. In a crab balance, your body should look like (1 mark)
   A. a snake
   B. a ball
   C. a spear
   D. a table

25. Good manners for an audience include (1 mark)
   A. walking around
   B. talking loudly
   C. throwing things
   D. being quiet and clapping at the right time

26. What does good diction mean? (1 mark)
   A. Singing with no words
   B. Saying the words clearly
   C. Clapping
   D. Singing very loudly

27. A sign that gets wider to the right means (1 mark)
   A. slow
   B. getting louder
   C. stop
   D. getting softer

28. At a wedding, we are most likely to hear (1 mark)
   A. work songs only
   B. funeral songs
   C. topical songs only
   D. marriage songs

29. Why delete poor photographs? (1 mark)
   A. To cool it
   B. To make the screen dark
   C. So memory is not filled up
   D. To break the camera

30. The lens of a camera (1 mark)
   A. lets light in
   B. keeps it cool
   C. stores photos
   D. gives power

31. What should you do before photographing someone? (1 mark)
   A. Ask their permission
   B. Shout at them
   C. Take it secretly
   D. Take photos of strangers only

32. If G is doh, then B is (1 mark)
   A. doh
   B. soh
   C. me
   D. ray

33. Of the notes B, A and G, which is the highest? (1 mark)
   A. G
   B. They are equal
   C. A
   D. B

34. In water tag, players (1 mark)
   A. push others
   B. run on the pool side
   C. hold others under water
   D. walk fast, not run, and tag gently

35. In the sit-and-slide entry, you should turn (1 mark)
   A. away from the wall
   B. to face the wall and hold the edge
   C. upside down
   D. to the deep end

36. Which game uses small sinking toys? (1 mark)
   A. Water tag
   B. Circle walk
   C. Treasure hunt
   D. Follow the leader

37. Learning about animals in games links to (1 mark)
   A. Space travel
   B. Agriculture
   C. Weather forecasts
   D. Swimming lessons only

38. The crab walk strengthens the (1 mark)
   A. ears
   B. arms, shoulders and tummy
   C. eyes
   D. hair

39. Which words describe how loud or soft a performance was? (1 mark)
   A. Pitch
   B. Dynamics
   C. Diction
   D. Tempo

40. When the anthem is sung, you should (1 mark)
   A. run
   B. stand straight and be quiet
   C. sit and talk
   D. play

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Describe how to blow to make a good tone. (3 marks)

42. State the length of a crotchet and of a quaver in beats. (2 marks)

43. State three occasions when the Kenya National Anthem is sung. (3 marks)

44. Explain how to analyse a folk song performance using its components. (5 marks)

45. Explain how you decide whether a percussion instrument is melodic or non-melodic. (3 marks)

46. What is stepwise motion? Give an example. (2 marks)

47. Why is colour classification important in painting? (2 marks)

48. Describe how you would improvise a rhythm to accompany a song. (4 marks)

49. How do you care for a paint brush? (3 marks)

50. Describe how to make a chest pass. (4 marks)

51. State three points to check when giving feedback to a friend playing the recorder. (3 marks)

52. Explain how to make a slab and a coil from clay. (3 marks)

53. Describe how to play the note G on the descant recorder and explain how to get a good tone. (5 marks)

54. Give the French rhythm names for a crotchet and a pair of quavers. (2 marks)

55. Name three types of Kenyan folk songs and say when each is sung. (3 marks)

56. Explain how to tie an overhand knot. (3 marks)

57. What is a sequence in gymnastics? Give an example. (3 marks)

58. Describe how to draw a drum with tonal value using the smudge technique. (4 marks)

59. Explain what tone or value means in a drawing. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #7 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — high notes
   Shorter bars vibrate faster and sound higher.

2. B — 30.5 metres
   A full court is 30.5 metres long and 15.25 metres wide.

3. D — Shake hands and thank them
   Fair play means being respectful whether you win or lose.

4. C — Turning on the landing foot without moving it
   A player keeps one foot down and turns on it.

5. B — Pushing another player
   Contact such as pushing is not allowed.

6. B — Mix flour and cold water to a smooth paste, then add hot water while stirring
   An adult adds hot water to thicken the smooth paste.

7. A — how light or dark a colour is
   Value is the lightness or darkness of a colour.

8. A — a
   The letter a sits between the baseline and the top of small letters.

9. C — the pattern of long and short sounds
   Rhythm is the pattern of sounds over the beat.

10. A — silence
   A rest tells the performer to stay silent for a time.

11. A — Four
   Ascender line, top of small letters, baseline and descender line make four.

12. B — g
   The tail of g goes below the baseline.

13. D — to the next note above or below
   Steps go to a neighbouring note.

14. B — a flat palm held level
   Me is shown with a flat, level hand.

15. C — a sloping palm
   Ray is a palm that slopes upward.

16. D — d
   Doh is the lowest of the three.

17. B — Roll a small piece between the palms or on a table
   Rolling back and forth makes a long even coil.

18. B — the middle of the front foot
   The medium start places the rear knee by the middle of the front foot.

19. A — So it does not hit anyone
   Keeping it high and away from the track avoids hitting people.

20. C — With care and respect, never letting it touch the ground
   Respect for the flag means caring for it.

21. D — Slow down gradually
   Slowing down gradually is safer.

22. C — Sit with knees bent and feet flat
   You start sitting with knees bent and feet flat.

23. B — Behind you, shoulder-width apart
   Hands go behind you, about shoulder-width apart.

24. D — a table
   Arms and legs are the table legs, and the body is the top.

25. D — being quiet and clapping at the right time
   The audience should listen respectfully.

26. B — Saying the words clearly
   Clear words help the audience understand the message.

27. B — getting louder
   An opening sign means the music grows louder.

28. D — marriage songs
   Marriage songs praise the couple and give good wishes.

29. C — So memory is not filled up
   Deleting saves space.

30. A — lets light in
   The lens gathers light for the picture.

31. A — Ask their permission
   Permission is polite and safe.

32. C — me
   G, A, B match d, r, m.

33. D — B
   Fewer covered holes give a higher note.

34. D — walk fast, not run, and tag gently
   No pushing.

35. B — to face the wall and hold the edge
   You hold the edge as you lower yourself in.

36. C — Treasure hunt
   Players pick up toys from the pool bottom.

37. B — Agriculture
   Agriculture teaches about animals.

38. B — arms, shoulders and tummy
   The body is held up by the arms and legs.

39. B — Dynamics
   Dynamics are loud and soft.

40. B — stand straight and be quiet
   Show respect.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Put the mouthpiece between the lips, take a deep breath, blow gently and steadily, and start each note with a soft too or doo.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: A crotchet is one beat and a quaver is half a beat.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: School assembly, Madaraka Day, Mashujaa Day, Jamhuri Day, sports events and other official ceremonies. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

44. (5 marks)
   Answer: Say the community of origin, the type or occasion, the message and mood, the roles of the soloist, chorus and instrumentalists, and the instruments used.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of five components.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Listen to the sounds. If it plays different notes, high and low, that make a tune, it is melodic. If it gives only a beat or one kind of sound, it is non-melodic.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for listening, 1 mark for melodic meaning, 1 mark for non-melodic meaning.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: Moving from a note to the next note above or below. For example, d to r.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: It helps us know which colours to mix to get others. It shows that only primary colours are needed to make all the other colours.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: Sing the song and find the beat by tapping. Play the beat on an instrument. Change to a pattern, such as two quick sounds and a long sound. Repeat it and change it at the end of a verse.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step, up to 4.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: Rinse when changing colour, wash with soap after use, shape the tip and store it flat or with hairs up. Never leave it standing on its hairs in water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: Hold the ball at chest height with both hands. Look at the partner. Step forward and straighten the arms, turning the thumbs down. The ball goes to the partner's chest.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid step.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: Correct notes, steady rhythm and rests, clear tone without squeaks, good posture. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: Flatten the clay with a rolling pin until even for a slab. Roll a small piece between palms for a coil.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the slab, 1 mark for the coil, 1 mark for even thickness.

53. (5 marks)
   Answer: Hold the recorder with the left hand at the top and the right at the bottom. Cover the thumb hole and holes 1, 2 and 3 with the pads of the left fingers. Put the mouthpiece between the lips and blow gently and steadily with a soft too.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for holding, thumb hole, three holes, mouthpiece and gentle breath.

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: Crotchet: taa. Pair of quavers: ta-te.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: Work songs during work, funeral songs when someone dies, naming songs when a baby is named, initiation songs at initiation, marriage songs at weddings, worship songs at worship. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each type with its occasion.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Make a loop with the cord. Pass the end through the loop. Pull both ends to tighten.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: A set of movements done in a fixed order. For example crab balance, lower to the mat, lie straight, side roll.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning, 2 marks for the correct example.

58. (4 marks)
   Answer: Draw the outline lightly. Shade the dark parts by pressing harder and the light parts by pressing lightly. Rub the shading with a finger or tissue to blend. Leave the brightest part white.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

59. (3 marks)
   Answer: Tone means how light or dark an area is. In a charcoal drawing, we can make tones from light grey to black by pressing lightly or hard.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for lightness or darkness, 1 mark for range of tones, 1 mark for charcoal pressure.
